subject: Next steps: Deployment mode selection for Acme Health migration
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: Deployment mode selection for Acme Health migration

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our discovery call about migrating your inference workloads off the legacy GPU cluster: 

Summary of requirements
- Peak concurrency: ~120 concurrent requests during batch processing windows; normal traffic ~20 RPS.
- Latency SLO for interactive features: 150–200ms p95.
- Data controls: PHI in some datasets, must be in a VPC or on-prem for certain models.
- Migration desire: move away from self-hosted transformer infra to reduce ops burden and cost.

Initial recommendation (based on priorities):
- Hybrid approach: Start with Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation for inference-critical endpoints; use Redwood Private (VPC) for any PHI workloads that require customer-managed networking.
- Hosted API could be used for non-PHI internal tooling and rapid iteration during early migration phases.

Concrete next steps
1) I will share Dedicated pricing and a proposed migration playbook by EOD Tue (attached).
2) Dev / Lauren — would you be able to run a 1-hour technical deep-dive next Wed to validate latency/quant profiles?
3) Samir — if this aligns, can you confirm the list of models and which endpoints will be PHI vs non-PHI?

Attachment: migration-playbook-v2.docx (DOCX, 220KB stub)

Thanks — happy to adjust based on your constraints.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

---
From: Samir Rao <samir@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: Deployment mode selection for Acme Health migration

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. High level: sounds right. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- PHI scope: only the "patient-summarizer" and "clinical-triage" endpoints will carry PHI; everything else is de-identified.
- Models: currently running a mix of open models on our cluster (Llama 2 variants) and some licensed commercial models via another API; we want to consolidate to a single inference platform if possible.
- Timeline: we’d like a migration pilot in Q1 (Jan) with full cutover by end of Q2.

Confirming: please send pricing for Dedicated + the VPC deployment checklist (we'll need compliance details).

Also looped Elena for procurement and engineering follow-up.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of AI Platforms | Acme Health
samir@acmehealth.com

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: Deployment mode selection for Acme Health migration (internal)

Thanks — noted. I can do the technical deep-dive next Wed 10/20 at 11am PT. Agenda I propose:
- Walk through sample traffic & sequence length distributions (they mentioned variable long sequences)
- Latency benchmarking for Dedicated vs Hosted for their model set (we'll bring p95 numbers)
- VPC/on-prem requirements and KMS integration checklist
- Migration staging plan (canary, shadowing their current cluster)

Marissa — I'll prepare an initial perf estimate (tokens/sec, expected concurrency per GPU) and a short slide of tradeoffs between Dedicated and Private for their PHI endpoints.

Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: Deployment mode selection for Acme Health migration

Samir / Elena —

Following up with the deliverables we discussed. Attached: Dedicated pricing deck and a short migration playbook. Key notes inline:
- Redwood Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, SLA for uptime, predictable throughput — best for latency-sensitive production endpoints.
- Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem): required for PHI or workloads needing customer-managed networking and KMS. There is an onboarding time (estimated 4–8 weeks depending on networking approvals).
- Hosted API: fastest time-to-value for non-PHI workloads, lower ops overhead, but does not satisfy customer-managed networking for PHI.

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf (PDF, 420KB stub)

Next actions
- Samir: please confirm which endpoints are PHI (patient-summarizer, clinical-triage).
- Elena: can we get a rough vendor onboarding timeline from procurement (are there specific legal/infosec steps we should prep for DocuSign)?
- Dev / Lauren: prep benchmarks and an initial migration runbook for Wed.

I’ll also put a short proposal in HubSpot with the pilot scope for your review.

Best,
Marissa

---
From: Samir Rao <samir@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmehealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: Deployment mode selection for Acme Health migration

Marissa / Dev —

All good — pilot scope looks fine. Confirming PHI endpoints: patient-summarizer, clinical-triage. Procurement (Elena) says vendor onboarding usually takes 2–3 weeks once we get the agreement; she will follow up with a checklist.

We’re happy to proceed with the Dedicated pilot for the non-PHI and use Private/VPC for the two PHI endpoints. Please go ahead and send the HubSpot proposal and a statement of work draft so procurement can start review.

Thanks,
Samir
